name: Create Application Wizard (Interactive Report page)
apex: Wizard step that adds an interactive report page while creating a new application, choosing a source, optional lookup columns, and an optional paired form page.
workflow: Add Page > Interactive Report inside Create Application Wizard; pick source, optional form and lookup columns, then Create Application.
relevance: Lookup Columns (swap an FK id for a display column) and the optional paired form page are patterns worth offering when wiring a Paddock table region to related data.

name: Create Page Wizard (Interactive Report page)
apex: Adds one interactive report page to an existing application, choosing a data source type and optionally a paired modal form page.
workflow: Create Page > Interactive Report, choose Data Source and Source Type, optionally enable breadcrumb/nav entries, then Create Page.
relevance: The Data Source picker (table vs SQL vs REST vs JSON vs sample) is exactly the abstraction a Paddock region needs when it can be backed by curated content, an API, or computed data.

name: Managing Interactive Report Attributes (overview)
apex: Table-of-contents page listing the attribute-editing subtopics for interactive reports: link columns, search bar, actions menu, download, pagination, icon/detail view, advanced.
relevance: Pure navigation page with no settings of its own; every setting is covered in its own linked subtopic.
skip_for_web: navigational index only, no distinct settings

name: Editing Interactive Report Attributes
apex: Standard Page Designer workflow: select a region, open its Attributes tab, and edit grouped, searchable, help-annotated settings in the Property Editor.
workflow: Select the region in Rendering, open Attributes, filter or jump to a group, edit values, Save or Save and Run Page.
relevance: The searchable, grouped property panel with inline per-field help is a UX pattern worth copying for Paddock Developer's own component-settings panel.

name: Search Bar
apex: The toolbar above an interactive report offering column-scoped search, an actions menu, a saved-report selector, and a view switcher when multiple views exist.
attributes: Finder Drop Down (Select columns to search)
workflow: In the region's Attributes > Search Bar group, toggle Include Search Bar and its sub-controls On/Off, or turn the whole bar Off.
relevance: Maps directly to a generic table/list region toolbar: free-text search, column-scoped search, saved-view dropdown, per-page count — all useful for Paddock standings/results tables.

name: Actions Menu
apex: Dropdown next to the search bar giving end users self-service report customization; the developer toggles which capabilities appear.
workflow: In the region Attributes > Actions Menu group, toggle each end-user capability On/Off; Off entries vanish from the menu entirely.
relevance: Per-capability toggles for end-user self-service (column show/hide, sort, save-view, filter) is the direct model for componentizing Paddock table controls instead of an all-or-nothing toolbar.

name: Download
apex: Actions-menu feature exporting the report as CSV, HTML, Excel, PDF, or an email attachment, with per-format options and an authorization gate.
workflow: Turn Actions Menu > Download On, pick Download Formats, optionally restrict with an authorization scheme, set CSV/email/filename details.
relevance: CSV/Excel export of standings and results tables is a plausible Paddock feature; the format-list-plus-authorization-gate pattern is directly reusable even though PDF/email need Oracle-specific infra.
skip_for_web: PDF and email download rely on an Oracle report server and instance-level SMTP config; a Next.js export would use its own code, not this infra.

name: Pagination
apex: Attributes controlling how a report pages through rows: the paging control style, where it displays, and the row ceiling.
workflow: In Attributes > Pagination, set Type, Display Position (above/below, left/right), and Maximum Rows to Display.
relevance: Standard pagination controls (style, position, max rows) map straight onto any Paddock table/list region.

name: Icon View
apex: Alternate card-grid display for a report: rows render as images with a label and link instead of table cells, toggled from the Search bar.
workflow: In Attributes > Icon View, turn Show On and pick link/image/label columns, or enable Custom and write a link template with #COLUMN# substitutions.
relevance: Essentially a driver/team/event card-grid toggle on the same data as the table view; matches Paddock's driver and team card layouts as an alternate view of one region.

name: Detail View
apex: Alternate stacked label/value display of each row, generated from an HTML template with before/each-row/after blocks and column substitution strings.
workflow: In Attributes > Detail View, turn Show On and write Before Rows / For Each Row / After Rows HTML using #COLUMN# substitution strings.
relevance: A templated per-row detail block is a good mobile/compact alternate view for Paddock driver or results rows; the same row-template idea (label:value stack) is worth exposing as a setting.

name: Advanced Attributes
apex: Region-level settings for stable external referencing: an alias to identify the region across exports, an item that stores the active saved-report ID, a report-specific email From address, and an Oracle Text search index column.
workflow: In Attributes > Advanced, set a unique Region Alias for stable API/URL references, plus optional email and text-index settings.
relevance: Region Alias — a stable developer-chosen name distinct from the volatile internal ID — is good practice for Paddock component identifiers used in URLs or APIs so exports/renames do not break links.
skip_for_web: Oracle Text Index Column and the report-level email From address are Oracle-DB/SMTP specific.

name: Interactive Report Filters (end-user)
apex: Filter chips shown between the search bar and report body once a user applies a search or filter; each chip is independently toggled, edited, or removed.
workflow: End user adds a filter via Actions menu or search; it appears as a chip they can check off, click to edit, collapse, or remove with the X icon.
relevance: Chip-style filter display with per-chip enable/edit/remove is a strong UI pattern for a Paddock filter region, e.g. season/team/driver filters on standings.

name: Saved Reports (Private/Public/Default/Alternative)
apex: System letting end users persist their own report customizations as Private or Public views, while developers separately save a Primary Default or named Alternative Default view; saved reports list in the Reports select list.
workflow: Actions menu > Report > Save Report; end users pick Public/Private, developers pick As Default Report Settings > Primary/Alternative; rename or delete via the saved report link.
relevance: A save-my-view feature (private to me vs shared publicly) is high value for Paddock power users customizing standings/results filters and worth designing as a first-class capability.

name: Linking to Interactive Reports (URL syntax)
apex: URL query syntax (Request, itemNames/itemValues with comparison operators, ClearCache) that deep-links into a specific saved report or applies a filter on page load.
attributes: itemNames/itemValues operators (C, EQ, GT, LIKE, IN, ROWFILTER, etc.)
workflow: Build a link with the report's DOM-qualified Request and filter item name/value pairs to open a saved report pre-filtered; add a ClearCache code to reset state.
relevance: The general idea of shareable URLs that open a saved view or preset filter/sort state, with named comparison operators, applies directly to Paddock's bookmarkable filtered table links even though the f?p/IR[] syntax itself is not reusable.
skip_for_web: The f?p URL syntax and region-DOM-ID qualification are APEX-internal plumbing a Next.js app would replace with its own query-string design.

name: Natural Language Support
apex: Lets end users type natural-language requests (filter, sort, highlight, group) against a report; a configured Generative AI Service translates the request into the report's existing declarative settings, plus a conversational AI Assistant panel.
attributes: Default Search Mode: Search with AI
workflow: Create a Generative AI Service, associate it with the app, enable Natural Language Support on the region, write Report Context and per-column Context/reference data, then end users type requests into the search bar or AI Assistant.
relevance: A natural-language box over standings/results (show only Ferrari drivers, highlight podiums) scoped to the report's own columns is a compelling AI feature; the guardrail of applying only existing settings (no open-ended analysis) is worth copying.

name: Classic Report (concept)
apex: A formatted display of a SQL query's results where, unlike interactive reports or grids, end users can only sort and do simple keyword search, not restructure columns, save views, or chart.
workflow: Developer selects a table or supplies a SQL SELECT; end users get search and column-header sorting only.
relevance: The plain-fixed-report vs richly-customizable-report distinction matters: not every Paddock table (e.g. a small driver bio list) needs a full toolbox; a lightweight sort+search-only variant fits simpler public pages.

name: Supported Columns in Classic Reports
apex: The fixed vocabulary of column display types available to any classic report column, set via the column's Identification > Type attribute.
attributes: Plain Text (based on List of Values)
workflow: Select the column in Page Designer and set Identification, Type to one of the supported column types.
relevance: This exact column-type vocabulary (rich text/markdown, image, download link, percent graph, hidden) is a strong starting list for Paddock's own generic table column-type registry.
skip_for_web: Download BLOB assumes DB blob storage; Paddock would use a file/asset URL column type instead.

name: Create Application Wizard (Classic Report page)
apex: Wizard step adding a classic report page while creating a new application; identical flow to the Interactive Report wizard (source, lookup columns, optional form, advanced flags) but produces a plain report.
workflow: Add Page > Classic Report inside Create Application Wizard.
relevance: Same wizard mechanics as the Interactive Report Create App Wizard already logged; only the resulting report type differs.
skip_for_web: Duplicate of the Interactive Report wizard entry; no new designer pattern.

name: Create Page Wizard (Classic Report page)
apex: Adds one classic report page to an existing application, with the same Data Source and Source Type choices as the Interactive Report Create Page Wizard.
workflow: Create Page > Classic Report, choose Data Source and Source Type, then Create Page.
relevance: Duplicate of the Interactive Report Create Page Wizard entry already logged; Data Source picker and navigation flags are identical.

name: Editing Classic Report Region Attributes
apex: Standard Page Designer workflow for editing a classic report's Region tab (source, layout, display selector, conditions) via the same grouped Property Editor pattern used elsewhere.
workflow: Select the region in Rendering, edit Region tab attributes, save.
relevance: Duplicate of the Property Editor / Filter Properties / Go to Group pattern already logged for Interactive Report attributes; only Region vs Attributes tab differs.
skip_for_web: Redundant with the earlier attribute-editing workflow entry.

name: Order By Item
apex: A region-level setting that builds an end-user select list (or other item) from developer-predefined ORDER BY clauses, letting users resort a region that has no built-in sort UI, such as a Cards region.
workflow: On the region's Region tab, set Order By Type to Item, then define named Clause/Key/Display rows in the Order By Item dialog; APEX generates a select list end users use to resort the region.
relevance: Exactly the sort-dropdown mechanism Paddock's card-style regions (driver/team cards) need: a developer-authored list of named sort options (Points descending, Alphabetical) users pick at runtime, without exposing arbitrary column sort.

name: Report Printing (print server configuration)
apex: Region- and app-level system exporting reports to PDF/Excel/RTF/HTML via a pluggable print-server backend (native, Oracle BI Publisher, APEX Office Print, Apache FOP, Document Generator), formatted with an XSL-FO or Office-template Report Layout.
attributes: Print Server Type: Remote Print Server
Print Server Type: Use Instance Settings
workflow: Set Print Server Type at the application level (or per-region Printing Enabled), attach a Report Layout, and let users trigger the configured export format.
relevance: The underlying want, export or print a standings/results table as a clean PDF, is plausible for Paddock, but the pluggable print-server / BI Publisher / XSL-FO machinery is pure Oracle infrastructure a Next.js app would replace with its own PDF library.
skip_for_web: External print server config (BI Publisher, APEX Office Print, Apache FOP, remote server credentials) is Oracle Administration Services infrastructure with no web equivalent to copy.

name: BLOB Support in Forms and Reports (Download BLOB / Display Image columns)
apex: Declarative column types that turn a database BLOB into a download link or an inline image, driven by a BLOB Attributes group naming the source table, BLOB column, primary key, mime type, filename, and last-updated columns.
workflow: Add a numeric file-size column to the report SQL, set its Type to Download BLOB or Display Image, then fill in the BLOB Attributes group naming the source table/columns.
relevance: The column-type concept itself (an image/file column with alt text and an inline-vs-download choice) is worth keeping in Paddock's column-type registry, even though the BLOB storage/retrieval plumbing does not apply.
skip_for_web: The whole mechanism assumes files live in an Oracle BLOB column; Paddock stores media in object storage (R2/Supabase) and would reference it by URL, not by table/column/primary-key lookup.

name: Lost Update Detection
apex: Concurrency guard on a form's automatic DML process that rejects a save if the underlying row changed since it was queried, preventing one user's edit from silently overwriting another's.
attributes: Lost Update Type: Row Version Column
Prevent Lost Updates (on Form - Automatic Row Processing (DML))
workflow: On the form region Attributes > Edit group, set Lost Update Type, then on the Form - Automatic Row Processing (DML) process set Prevent Lost Updates to On.
relevance: Any multi-admin editing surface in Paddock Developer (the page designer itself, content editing) needs exactly this: detect a stale save and refuse it rather than clobbering a concurrent edit, the same principle already used for this project's own file-edit-since-read guard.

name: BLOB Support in Forms (File Browse)
apex: Declarative file upload/download on a form item bound to a BLOB column, with a File Browse item type, a choice of storage location (permanent column vs auto-purged temp storage), and companion columns for mime type, filename, last-updated and charset.
attributes: Storage Type: BLOB column in Item Source Attribute
workflow: Point a File Browse item at a BLOB column (or temp storage), add companion metadata columns to the base table, and wire a Remove button that nulls all of them together.
relevance: The storage-type split (permanent vs auto-purged temporary upload) and storing mime/filename/last-updated alongside a file are patterns worth reusing for any Paddock media/asset upload feature, and the remove-reference button pattern is needed for unlinking media.
skip_for_web: The BLOB-column mechanics themselves do not apply; Paddock would store files in object storage (R2/Supabase) and keep only a URL plus the same metadata fields.

name: Oracle JET Integration
apex: Background architecture note: APEX bundles the Oracle JET JavaScript toolkit (used mainly by the Chart region) via a RequireJS module loader, pre-optimized into minified bundles that load only when a Chart or Interactive Grid needing charts is actually on the page, falling back to unbundled files in Debug mode.
workflow: Not developer-configured directly; APEX auto-loads jetCommonBundle.min.js and chartBundle.min.js only when a page includes a Chart region.
relevance: The lazy-load-heavy-vendor-library-only-when-used pattern, with an unbundled debug fallback, is a real engineering lesson for Paddock Developer if its own designer ships a heavy charting/mapping library: do not ship it on every page.
skip_for_web: The specific RequireJS/bundle-file mechanism is Oracle Application Express plumbing, not something to copy literally in a Next.js build.

name: Sample Calendar (example app)
apex: A sample Monthly Calendar built on a projects/orders table, demonstrating the baseline calendar UX: month navigation plus a switch between calendar and list rendering of the same events.
workflow: Install the Sample Calendar app from the App Gallery to see a working monthly calendar with a List view toggle.
relevance: Paddock already has a race calendar; the Month/List view toggle plus Previous/Next navigation is exactly the baseline UX its calendar component needs.

name: Create Application Wizard (Calendar page)
apex: Wizard step that adds a calendar page to a new application by mapping a table's columns to the event title and date range.
workflow: Add Page > Calendar; pick the source table, then map Display/Start Date/End Date columns and toggle Show Time.
relevance: The calendar's minimum required schema, a title column plus start date and optional end date for duration events, with Show Time gating Week/Day views, is the exact settings shape Paddock's own calendar component (race weekends, sessions) should expose.

name: Create Page Wizard (Calendar page)
apex: Adds one calendar page to an existing application, choosing a Data Source then mapping the same Display/Start Date/End Date/Show Time attributes as the Create Application Wizard.
workflow: Create Page > Calendar, choose Data Source and Source Type, then map calendar column attributes.
relevance: Duplicates the calendar column-mapping already logged from the Create Application Wizard entry, plus the generic Data Source picker logged for reports.

name: Dynamic Action Support for Calendar
apex: Three calendar-specific client-side events a developer can wire a Dynamic Action to, each passing a data payload, letting other regions react to calendar interaction without custom JavaScript.
workflow: Create a Dynamic Action on the Calendar page, set When > Event to one of the three calendar events, then define actions (e.g. refresh a report) that read the emitted data payload.
relevance: Exactly the interaction Paddock needs: clicking a date or event on the race calendar, or changing its view, should be able to drive another region (refresh a sessions list, highlight a race weekend) via a declared event and payload rather than bespoke glue code per page.

name: Sample Charts (example app)
apex: A sample bar chart demonstrating multi-series display: two stacked series on the primary Y axis and a third series plotted separately on a secondary Y axis, with runtime toggles.
workflow: Install the Sample Charts app to see toggles that flip orientation and stacking on a live multi-series bar chart.
relevance: Paddock will chart things like points progression or lap-time comparison across drivers; the stack/unstack and secondary-axis patterns are directly useful for comparing multiple drivers or metrics on one chart.

name: Create Application Wizard (Chart page)
apex: Wizard step adding a chart page to a new application by picking a chart type and mapping a table's columns to an x-axis label and an aggregated value.
workflow: Add Page > Chart, choose a chart type, map Label Column (x-axis) and Value Column with an aggregation, then Add Page; a Dashboard page can bundle up to four charts.
relevance: This label-column plus aggregated-value-column model, with Sum/Count/raw-value aggregation, is exactly the data-binding shape Paddock's own chart component needs for standings progression, points-per-race, or lap-time comparisons.

name: Create Page Wizard (Chart page)
apex: Adds one chart page to an existing application via the same Data Source picker used by other regions, then chart-type-specific attributes that vary by the chart type chosen.
workflow: Create Page > Chart, pick chart type and Data Source, then fill in the type-specific chart attributes.
relevance: Duplicates the Data Source picker already logged; the chart-specific Label/Value/Aggregation attributes are already captured from the Create Application Wizard entry.

name: Sample Maps (example app)
apex: Two example map pages: a single-layer map of country polygons with name tooltips, and a two-layer map combining a heat map of point density with a polygon layer underneath.
workflow: Install the Sample Maps app to see one-layer and two-layer map pages built on local tables.
relevance: The layered composition model, a base layer plus an overlay heat map or point layer, is worth copying for a Paddock circuits/venues map even without a spatial database backing it.

name: Create Application Wizard (Map page)
apex: Wizard step adding a map page to a new application, built only on a local table, choosing a spatial layer type and how coordinates are sourced.
attributes: Geometry Column Type: Two Numeric Columns (longitude/latitude)
workflow: Add Page > Map, select a table, pick a layer type (Points, Lines, Polygons, Heat Map, Extruded Polygons) and a geometry source, then map the required columns.
relevance: A Points layer sourced from Two Numeric Columns (plain longitude/latitude, no spatial database) is exactly the minimal map Paddock needs for circuit locations or a season map; GeoJSON-based Polygon/Line layers are the option for track-outline overlays.
skip_for_web: SDO_GEOMETRY and CLOB/VARCHAR2 geometry-column sourcing assume an Oracle spatial datatype; Paddock would only need the plain lon/lat path.

name: Create Page Wizard (Map page)
apex: Adds a map page from a broader set of sources than the Create Application Wizard (local DB, REST Enabled SQL, REST Source, JSON Source), with the same layer-type and geometry-source choices, plus an option to combine the map with a Faceted Search region.
workflow: Create Page > Map, pick a Data Source (including REST/JSON, unlike the app wizard), set Map Style and Geometry Column Type, optionally enable Create a Faceted Search Page.
relevance: Confirms a map region can be driven by an external REST/JSON source rather than only a DB table, matching how Paddock would feed a map from its own curated venue JSON; the map-plus-faceted-search combo suits a filter-circuits-by-region-and-see-them-on-a-map page.

name: Map Backgrounds (Shared Component)
apex: A reusable named basemap definition, Vector Tile, Raster XYZ Tile, or OGC WMS layer, stored once in Shared Components and applied to any Map region, Display Map item, or Geocoded Address item in the app.
attributes: URL to Map Stylesheet / Raster Tiles (XYZ) URL / WMS URL
workflow: Shared Components > Map Backgrounds > Create; pick a Type, paste the provider's tile/style URL (with an {api-key} placeholder if needed), then reference this background by name wherever a map is used.
relevance: Exactly the shared-basemap abstraction Paddock needs: define a MapTiler/Mapbox tile source once, with its API key, and reuse it across every circuit or venue map instead of hardcoding a tile URL per region.

name: Map Background Dark Mode and Credentialed API Key
apex: Per-background attributes letting one basemap definition swap tile layers for dark mode and source its API key from a scoped Web Credential instead of a plaintext value.
attributes: Web Credential Valid for URLs: browser:// entry
Web Credential Valid for URLs: https:// entry
workflow: On the Map Background edit page, set a separate Dark Mode tile layer and switch API Key sourcing to a Web Credential scoped to the specific app page and map-server URL.
relevance: A light/dark tile-layer pair driven by the site's own theme toggle is directly reusable since Paddock already needs light/dark parity everywhere; storing a map API key as a scoped credential rather than inline is good secrets practice to mirror.

name: Using Custom Map Backgrounds
apex: The three places a saved background can be attached: a Map region's Background attribute, a Display Map item's Background setting, and Component Settings > Geocoded Address's Background, each offering Default/Built-In/Shared Component choices.
attributes: Display Map item Settings, Custom Background
Geocoded Address Component Settings, Custom Background
workflow: On a Map region, Display Map item, or the Geocoded Address component setting, set Background to Shared Component and pick the saved Map Background.
relevance: Confirms one shared basemap can back several different map-shaped components consistently, a pattern worth mirroring if Paddock ends up with more than one map-shaped component, e.g. a full circuit map versus a small location indicator on a driver card.

name: Map Background CRUD (delete, copy, reports)
apex: Standard Shared Component maintenance screens for a map background: delete, copy to a new name (or from another app), and Utilization/History reports.
workflow: From Shared Components > Map Backgrounds, open a background to Delete it, use its row Copy icon to duplicate it, or view the Utilization/History tabs.
relevance: Identical generic Shared Component CRUD pattern (create/edit/delete/copy/utilization/history) already established for other shared components such as Lists and LOVs; no new designer concept.
skip_for_web: Routine CRUD chrome, not a distinct feature to copy.

name: Creating Help for Your Application
apex: Built-in system for authoring page-level and item-level help text, reviewing or bulk-seeding it app-wide via a report, and linking to a dedicated Help page that shows help for whatever page the user was just on.
workflow: Add a Help Text region and set Page Help Text / Item Help attributes per page; review or seed all of it app-wide from Utilities > Item Utilities > Edit Item Help Text; link to it via a nav-bar entry passing &APP_PAGE_ID.
relevance: Paddock Developer's own component-settings panel should carry per-field help text plus one report to review all field help across the app; the current-page-aware help link is a good contextual-help pattern to copy for the designer's own admin UI.

name: Managing Themes and Subscriptions (overview)
apex: Table-of-contents page for theme lifecycle tasks: editing, switching, ID changes, copying, deleting, instance-level theme repository, export/import, and reports.
relevance: Pure navigation page; substantive theme-subscription mechanics are covered in the linked subtopic.
skip_for_web: navigational index only

name: Theme Subscriptions
apex: A distribution model where an app's theme stays locked to a master theme so Oracle can push template upgrades in future releases; a developer can locally fork one template or style to make it editable, at the cost of excluding just that piece from future refreshes.
attributes: Re-subscribe (change ID, recreate, switch, delete original)
Local template copy (breaks subscription for that template only)
workflow: An app subscribes automatically when created from a built-in theme; Verify checks drift from the master, Refresh pulls updates, or Unsubscribe/copy-locally to freeze specific pieces.
relevance: This solves distributing one master theme to many separate customer applications with selective override, a multi-tenant packaging problem Paddock does not have; its one Next.js codebase versions its whole design system in git instead.
skip_for_web: No multi-application theme distribution exists to manage; git branches already give Paddock the equivalent of subscribe/fork per file.

name: Accessing New Themes (Create Theme Wizard)
apex: Adds an additional theme to an application, sourced from the instance theme repository, copied from another application, built from scratch, or imported from an export.
attributes: As a copy from another application
workflow: Shared Components > Themes > Create, pick a creation method, follow the wizard.
relevance: Multi-theme-per-app and cross-application theme copying address running many differently-branded APEX apps off one repository; Paddock is a single site with one design system.

name: Theme ID / Copy / Delete utilities
apex: Maintenance utilities for a theme's numeric ID: renumber it (for export to another app), duplicate it under a new ID for safe experimentation, or delete an inactive one.
workflow: Shared Components > Themes > Tasks list > Change Identification Number / Copy Theme / Delete Theme.
relevance: Renumbering and duplicating themes exists to move a theme between separate APEX applications; Paddock's one design system lives in one git repo with no equivalent ID-collision problem.

name: Creating a Master Theme Application
apex: A dedicated application whose sole purpose is holding one theme so other applications can subscribe to it as their shared source of truth.
attributes: Copy Existing App: Copy From, Copy To, New Application ID
Copy a theme and subscribe, then switch to it
workflow: Start from a Universal Theme-based sample app, or copy an existing app's theme and subscribe, then switch other apps onto it.
relevance: Solves sharing one design system across many separate APEX applications; Paddock already has a single source of truth by having one codebase, so no separate master-theme app is needed.

name: Managing Instance Themes
apex: Instance-administrator-only capability to add or remove themes from the Oracle APEX instance-wide public Theme repository.
relevance: Requires an Instance Administrator role over a shared multi-workspace APEX install; Paddock has no equivalent instance-level admin tier or public theme repository.
skip_for_web: Out of scope: instance-level administration, not application design.

name: Exporting and Importing Themes
apex: Moves a theme between separate APEX development instances by exporting it as part of an application export file, then importing and installing it in the target instance.
workflow: Create an app using the theme, export it, import the file into the target instance, install from the Export Repository.
relevance: Solves moving a theme between separate installations; Paddock's equivalent transport is git, which already moves the whole design system atomically.

name: Viewing Theme Reports
apex: Five cross-cutting reports over a theme: every template it contains, template counts per class, every file referenced by templates/components, every CSS class referenced by templates/components, and every supported substitution string.
workflow: Shared Components > Themes > Reports, pick a report type and a theme scope, click Go; File/Class References can download as CSV.
relevance: The File References and Class References reports, where is this asset or CSS class used across every template and component, are a genuinely useful impact-analysis pattern worth copying for Paddock Developer's own designer before removing a shared component or style.
skip_for_web: The template-count and substitution-string reports are theme-packaging bookkeeping specific to APEX's template system.

name: Calling the JavaScript File from the Page Template
apex: Best practice of referencing a shared .js file from the page template shell so it loads once on first view and is then browser-cached across the whole application.
workflow: Add a script reference to the page template rather than inlining JavaScript per page.
relevance: Next.js layouts plus its bundler already deliver this outcome automatically (shared code split once, cached across routes); there is no equivalent manual step to add to Paddock Developer's plan.
skip_for_web: Solved structurally by the framework already in use.

name: Escaping Syntax in Substitution Strings
apex: Appending !FILTERNAME to a substitution string (e.g. &ITEM!HTML.) to escape special characters and prevent XSS when the value is rendered.
workflow: Append ! plus a predefined filter name to any &SUBSTITUTION. reference that outputs user-controlled data.
relevance: Duplicate of output-escaping already logged from the Concepts chapter; React/JSX auto-escapes interpolated content by default, so this manual per-substitution escape syntax addresses a problem Paddock's stack does not have outside dangerouslySetInnerHTML.

name: Selecting a Default Page Template
apex: A page's template resolves from a theme-wide default (Component Defaults > Page) unless a specific page overrides it in its own Appearance > Page Template attribute.
workflow: Set the app-wide default under Shared Components > Themes > Component Defaults; override per page in Page Designer's Appearance group if a page needs a different shell.
relevance: Confirms the cascading-default-with-per-instance-override pattern, a global default template overridable per page, that Paddock Developer's own Component Settings feature already implements; validates that existing design.

name: Viewing Template Reports
apex: Interactive report over all templates in the app with tabs for subscription status, publishing master-template changes to subscribers, per-template usage counts, and edit history.
workflow: Shared Components > Templates, then switch between Subscription/Publish/Utilization/History tabs; Utilization shows how many pages reference each template.
relevance: The per-template usage count (how many pages use this template) is a useful design-system health metric worth exposing in Paddock Developer: know how many regions use a given component template before changing or retiring it.
skip_for_web: The Subscription and Publish tabs are the multi-app theme-distribution mechanic already judged not applicable.

name: Label Templates
apex: A centrally managed HTML wrapper applied to every form item's label, input, help, and inline-error markup, selectable per item so, for example, a Required Field variant can prepend an asterisk image everywhere it is used.
workflow: Define a Label Template's Before/After Label, Item, Error, and Field Container HTML once with substitution strings, then assign it to any item needing that label style.
relevance: The centrally templated field wrapper, label plus input plus help plus inline error, selectable per item (e.g. a Required-Field variant), is the exact Field component contract Paddock Developer's own form-building component should offer instead of hardcoding label/error markup per form.

name: Popup LOV Templates
apex: A single per-theme template controlling the layout of the legacy popup picker window used by items of type POPUP: its search field, Find/Close/Next/Previous buttons, raw browser-window sizing, pagination, and result-set wrapper.
attributes: Search Field: Before/After Field Text, Filter Width
workflow: Edit the theme's one Popup List of Values Template to restyle the search box, buttons, and popup window used by every POPUP item.
relevance: The reusable value-picker-dialog idea is already captured by the List of Values entries logged earlier; the raw browser popup-window mechanics (scrollbars=, resizable=) are legacy plumbing a modern modal/combobox component would not use.
skip_for_web: Raw window.open-style popup sizing has no place in a modern SPA design system.

name: Template Component Type Plug-ins
apex: A Template Component is a plug-in wrapping one HTML template plus template directives; if it belongs to a theme it lives under Templates, if standalone it lives under Plug-ins, and either can be copied from another application's theme into the current one.
workflow: Shared Components > Plug-ins > Create > As a Copy of an Existing Plug-in, pick the source application/theme and template, name the copy.
relevance: This packages a template as a portable unit for copying between separate APEX applications; Paddock's single codebase shares components directly in source rather than needing a plug-in copy mechanism.

name: Optimizing a Page for Printing (Printer Friendly template)
apex: A dedicated alternate page template that strips navigation chrome and renders form items as plain text, selectable as the theme default and toggled at runtime via a URL flag.
attributes: Theme, Component Defaults, Printer Friendly Page
workflow: Create or select a Printer Friendly page template under the theme's Component Defaults, then add the PrinterFriendly flag to a link or nav icon to render that mode.
relevance: A dedicated chrome-stripped print variant, toggled by a URL flag, is a nice pattern for a printable Paddock standings/results view, implementable with print CSS or a query-flagged route variant rather than APEX's specific mechanism.
skip_for_web: The f?p syntax itself does not apply.

name: Creating a Region from the Gallery
apex: The drag-and-drop or right-click component palette in Page Designer's Layout tab, grouped into Regions/Items/Buttons, that inserts a new component at a chosen or dropped location with live valid-drop-target highlighting.
attributes: Messages icon (error list linking to the Property Editor)
workflow: Open the Gallery under the Layout tab, drag a component onto a highlighted valid drop zone (or right-click > Add To), then fix any listed errors via the Messages icon.
relevance: This is the exact palette-drag-drop-with-valid-drop-target-highlighting interaction Paddock Developer's own designer canvas needs: a grouped component gallery developers drag onto the layout, with an error list linking each problem straight to the offending attribute.

name: About Managing Images
apex: Images must be uploaded to a static file repository before they can be referenced in an application, scoped at upload time as either available to all applications or restricted to one specific application.
workflow: Upload the image file once, choosing workspace-wide or single-app availability, then reference it by its file path in region/item HTML.
relevance: Validates the two-tier shared-vs-scoped asset model worth keeping for Paddock's own media library: some images (logos, team colors) are global, others belong to one page or content item.
skip_for_web: The specific upload-to-database-repository mechanism does not apply; Paddock already stores media in object storage (R2/Supabase).

name: Rendering HTML Using Custom PL/SQL
apex: An escape-hatch region type that runs procedural code (PL/SQL Web Toolkit htp.p calls, with session-state bind variables) to produce arbitrary HTML when no built-in region type covers the need, at the cost of losing template consistency.
workflow: Create a region of type PL/SQL and write htp.p() calls that emit HTML directly, querying tables or session state as needed.
relevance: Every declarative page builder needs an acknowledged escape hatch, a Custom Code region for content the component library does not cover, with an explicit warning that it forfeits the design system's consistency; Paddock Developer should offer the same trade-off rather than pretend every layout fits the component model.

name: Viewing Page Items (Property Editor)
apex: Standard Page Designer workflow for selecting a page item in Rendering or Layout and editing its grouped attributes in the Property Editor.
workflow: Select the item, filter or browse to an attribute group, edit values, save.
relevance: Duplicate of the Property Editor pattern already logged multiple times for regions and reports.

name: Creating a Page Item from the Rendering Tab
apex: Two right-click entry points for adding a new form field to a region: Create Page Item on the region itself, or Create Page Item Below an existing item, both landing on the same Property Editor with a green marker flagging unsaved fields.
attributes: Create Page Item Below (on existing item)
workflow: Right-click a region or an existing item in Rendering, choose Create Page Item (Below), name it, set its Type, then fill in the rest of the Property Editor.
relevance: The unsaved-field green-marker affordance is a small but genuinely useful UI nugget for Paddock Developer's own settings panel: show the developer exactly which fields changed since the last save.

name: Adding a Page Item from the Gallery
apex: Drag-and-drop or right-click Add To insertion of a new form field from the Gallery's Items tab, with the same error-highlighting Messages dialog used for regions.
workflow: Open the Gallery Items tab, drag an item type onto the layout or right-click Add To, then resolve any listed errors.
relevance: Duplicate of the Gallery drag-and-drop and Messages-dialog pattern already logged for regions; only the target component kind (item vs region) differs.

name: Shuttle Item
apex: A dual-listbox form control that lets a user move values between an Available column and a Selected column, backed by a list of values plus a multi-row SQL source collapsed into one delimited item value.
attributes: List of Values, Type: SQL Query
Source, Type: SQL Query (return multiple values)
workflow: Set an item's Type to Shuttle, point List of Values at a SQL query for the available options, point Source at a multi-row query for the current selection, and set the Multiple Values separator.
relevance: A real, reusable multi-select control Paddock's own admin/designer needs, e.g. assigning several drivers to a team, several tags to a blog post, or several sessions to a race weekend, via move-between-columns rather than a cramped multi-select dropdown.

name: Deleting a Dynamic Action
apex: Removes a dynamic action via right-click Delete in the Dynamic Actions tab of Page Designer.
workflow: Open Dynamic Actions, expand the event, right-click the action, Delete, Save.
relevance: Routine CRUD on a component already covered by the calendar dynamic-action entry; no new concept.

name: Incorporating JavaScript into an Application (guidance)
apex: Design guidance that client-side JavaScript suits lightweight interactive behavior but not data-intensive checks, since validating against a large table client-side would require downloading the whole table; heavy logic belongs in server-side validation instead.
relevance: A direct design guideline for Paddock Developer's own client-side rules or dynamic-action equivalent: keep them to UI behavior (show/hide, formatting) and push anything needing real data lookups server-side.

name: Creating a Breadcrumb While Creating a Page
apex: Wizard-time flags that give a new page a breadcrumb entry and/or a navigation menu entry, each defaulting its label to the page name and requiring a parent entry to place it in the hierarchy.
attributes: Breadcrumb Parent Entry (or - No parent entry -)
workflow: During Create Page, expand Navigation and enable Use Breadcrumb and/or Use Navigation, then pick each one's parent entry.
relevance: Confirms the parent-entry breadcrumb/nav-tree model, each page names its parent and defaults its label to the page name, that Paddock Developer's page hierarchy and auto-generated breadcrumbs should follow.

name: Accessing Breadcrumb Reports
apex: Three report tabs on the Breadcrumbs shared-component page: a spreadsheet-style Grid Edit to rename every breadcrumb entry at once, a Utilization report listing breadcrumbs by page, and a History of recent changes.
workflow: Shared Components > Breadcrumbs, switch to Grid Edit to bulk-edit names, or Utilization/History to review usage and changes.
relevance: The Grid Edit bulk-editor, rename many rows of a shared list at once in a spreadsheet-like table, is a reusable idea for Paddock Developer's own navigation/page-title management instead of opening each page individually.

name: Managing a Classic Navigation Bar
apex: A legacy image/text navigation bar system for applications on older themes, rendered wherever a page template includes the #NAVIGATION_BAR# substitution string; superseded by Navigation Menus for the Universal Theme.
attributes: Target: URL or Page in this Application
Request, Clear Cache, Set these items/With these values
workflow: Shared Components > Classic Navigation Bar Entries > Create, choose From Scratch or copy an existing entry, set its target and display attributes.
relevance: APEX's own documentation marks this superseded by Navigation Menus for current themes; Paddock's navigation is a single modern nav component, not a legacy image-bar system to emulate.
skip_for_web: Explicitly legacy per the source material itself.

name: Page Processes
apex: A server-side action attached to a specific point in the page lifecycle, with a pluggable executor type (run PL/SQL code, generate text with AI, invoke a PL/SQL package/procedure or a REST Source operation), plus declared success and error messaging.
attributes: Identification, Type: Generate Text with AI
Error, Display Location: Inline in Notification
Error, Display Location: On Error Page
workflow: Right-click a node in Processing or Rendering, Create Process, pick a Type (code/AI/API call), set when it runs (Sequence, Point, button condition), and define its success/error messages and where errors display.
relevance: The pluggable action-type model, run code, call a REST operation, or call AI, tied to a lifecycle point with a declared success message and an inline-vs-page error display choice, is the right shape for Paddock Developer's own on-submit action step for its handful of forms.

name: Editing Page Processes
apex: The same process attributes (Sequence, Point, Run Process, Server-side Condition, Success/Error messages) revisited via the standard Property Editor edit path rather than at creation time.
workflow: Processing tab > select an existing process > edit its grouped attributes > Save.
relevance: Duplicate of the Creating Page Processes entry; same attributes, only reached via editing an existing process instead of the creation wizard.

name: Supported Map Background Types
apex: The three tile-layer source formats a custom map background can wrap: a Vector Tile Layer (style.json URL), a Raster XYZ Tile Layer (URL taking x/y/z), or an OGC WMS layer (Web Map Service URL).
workflow: Pick one of the three types when defining a Map Background; each expects a differently shaped provider URL.
relevance: Confirms the three tile-source shapes (vector style, raster XYZ, WMS) a Paddock map basemap picker should support when wiring up a real tile provider like MapTiler or Mapbox.

name: Create Map Background Wizard
apex: The wizard fields for defining a new Map Background: its name, a stable Static ID, its tile-source Type, an optional API Key, and the provider URL, whose exact label and required parameters change based on Type.
attributes: WMS auto-added params excluded: BBOX, WIDTH, HEIGHT, REQUEST, FORMAT, SRS/CRS
workflow: Shared Components > Map Backgrounds > Create; name it, pick Type, paste the provider URL (using {api-key} if needed), noting the map region auto-supplies certain WMS parameters.
relevance: The auto-supplied WMS parameters, which the developer must not hardcode into the URL, is a specific integration detail worth remembering if Paddock ever wires up a WMS-based layer; the {api-key} placeholder substitution is a clean way to store a provider key once.

name: Copying a Custom Map Background
apex: Duplicates an existing map background under a new unique name, either from the Map Backgrounds report row or while running the Create wizard against another application.
workflow: Map Backgrounds page > row Copy icon > enter New Map Background Name > Copy Map Background.
relevance: Routine duplicate-with-new-name CRUD, same pattern already logged for other shared components.

name: Map Background Utilization and History Reports
apex: Two tabs on the Map Backgrounds page: Utilization shows where a background is used across the application, History shows recent edits to it.
workflow: Map Backgrounds page > Utilization or History tab.
relevance: Same generic usage/history reporting pattern already logged for other shared components such as Themes and Templates.

name: Copying a Theme
apex: Duplicates a theme under a new numeric ID within the current application, with the option to subscribe the copy to a master theme.
workflow: Shared Components > Themes > Tasks > Copy Theme, pick the source theme and a new ID, choose whether to subscribe.
relevance: Solves duplicating a theme for safe experimentation or renumbering before export between separate APEX applications; not applicable to Paddock's single git-versioned design system.

name: Deleting a Theme
apex: Removes an inactive theme's templates from the application; any un-exported template customizations on it are permanently lost.
workflow: Shared Components > Themes > Tasks > Delete Theme, select the theme, confirm.
relevance: Routine deletion CRUD for a multi-theme-per-app model Paddock does not have.

name: Display Image Item and Remove Image Pattern (Forms)
apex: A declarative Display Image item type renders a form's BLOB as an inline image; because File Browse has no way to clear a value, removing an image requires a dedicated button that nulls the image column and all its companion metadata columns together.
attributes: Nullify image + mimetype + filename + last-update + charset columns together
workflow: Use Display Image for the BLOB item's Type to show it inline; add a separate button whose process sets the BLOB and all companion columns to NULL to let users clear it.
relevance: The remove-reference pattern, one action clearing the file plus every piece of metadata describing it, is exactly what Paddock needs for an unlink/remove-media control on any image-backed field.
skip_for_web: The Display Image item's BLOB rendering itself does not apply; Paddock would swap in an image bound to a stored URL.

name: Procedural BLOB Access and Other Declarative Download Options
apex: An alternative to the built-in Download BLOB/Display Image column types: call APEX_UTIL.GET_BLOB_FILE_SRC directly for finer control over image sizing, or use built-in processes/dynamic-action plug-ins for simple SQL-driven downloads outside a report.
workflow: Call GET_BLOB_FILE_SRC from a valid APEX session when a column-type approach cannot express the needed image sizing; or attach a download process/dynamic action for one-off SQL-based downloads.
relevance: Every option here is a different way to stream an Oracle BLOB; Paddock's file downloads would instead link directly to an object-storage URL.
skip_for_web: Entirely BLOB-streaming-specific.

name: Report Queries and Report Layouts
apex: A Report Query is a Shared Component (built on a table, SQL query, or REST Data Source) that exists purely to be printed or exported, independent of any on-screen report region; a Report Layout, an XSL-FO or Office template, formats either a report region or a Report Query for printer-friendly output.
attributes: Report Query source: REST Data Source
workflow: Define a Report Query as a Shared Component pointing at a data source, attach a Report Layout to format it, then trigger it independently of any on-page region.
relevance: A reusable, region-independent export definition, decoupled from any specific on-screen table, is a good pattern for a Paddock export-standings-as-PDF feature not tied to whichever component renders it on screen.
skip_for_web: The XSL-FO/Office template formatting mechanism itself is Oracle print-server infrastructure.

name: Remote Print Server Setup
apex: A wizard for registering an external print server (Oracle Analytics Publisher or APEX Office Print) at the application level, including its endpoint URL and a paired Web Credential for authentication.
attributes: Print Server Type: Oracle Analytics Publisher
Print Server Type: APEX Office Print
workflow: Application Definition > Report Printing > Add Remote Print Server; pick the server type, enter its endpoint and host name, then create or select a Web Credential for it.
relevance: Registering an external Oracle-ecosystem print service with its own credential object is infrastructure Paddock has no equivalent for; any PDF export it builds would call its own code directly.

name: Native PDF and Excel Printing Limitations
apex: Built-in (no external print server) PDF and Excel export has hard limits: a PDF row can span at most one page break before truncating, and an Excel cell truncates past 32k characters.
relevance: A narrow Oracle-native-renderer limitation; a Next.js PDF/Excel export library would have its own separate limits, not these.

name: View Selector (Report/Icon/Detail/Chart/Group By)
apex: When more than one view is configured for a report, a view-selection button group appears in the search bar letting the end user switch between the default Report view and any enabled Icon, Detail, Chart, or Group By views of the same underlying data.
workflow: Enable more than one view (e.g. Icon View and Detail View) on the region; APEX automatically adds a view-switcher button group to the search bar.
relevance: A single dataset rendered as multiple interchangeable views (table, cards, detail-stack, chart) with one switcher control is precisely the multi-view region concept Paddock Developer should offer, e.g. toggling a driver list between table and card layouts.

name: CSV Download Specifics
apex: Fine-grained control over CSV export formatting: a custom column separator and enclosing-quote character, gated behind an Automatic CSV Encoding globalization setting.
workflow: Enable Automatic CSV Encoding on Edit Globalization Attributes first, then select CSV under Download Formats and set Separator/Enclosed By as needed.
relevance: Custom delimiter and quote-character controls matter if Paddock ever exports data for spreadsheet tools with different locale conventions.

name: Email Download Specifics
apex: Lets an authenticated end user send the current report download as an email attachment; requires instance-level SMTP configuration, excludes Word/RTF format, and always appends a system-generated sender signature that cannot be removed.
attributes: Authenticated users only (hidden on public pages)
workflow: Enable Send as Email under Download once SMTP is configured instance-wide; the option is hidden entirely on public, unauthenticated pages.
relevance: Emailing a report attachment straight from a data table is a fairly specific enterprise-report feature; Paddock's few forms and read-heavy pages have no equivalent send-as-email requirement today.
skip_for_web: Requires Oracle instance-level SMTP administration.

name: Email From Address Resolution
apex: The From address for interactive report emails resolves at two levels: an application-wide Application Email From Address, overridable per report via the region's own Email from Address advanced attribute; both accept a literal address or an app-level substitution, but per-item substitutions are discouraged since they only work for downloads, not subscriptions.
workflow: Set a default at Edit Application Definition, optionally override it per report under Attributes, Advanced, Email from Address.
relevance: A two-tier email-sender-address fallback is a narrow email-infrastructure detail; Paddock has no per-report emailing feature to configure this for.

name: Include Form Page defaults to Modal Dialog
apex: When a Create Page wizard's Include Form Page flag is enabled alongside a report, the generated companion form page is always created as a Modal Dialog page, never a full navigable page.
workflow: Enable Include Form Page while creating a report page; the paired form is created as a modal automatically, with no separate type choice.
relevance: Confirms modal-dialog-by-default is the right pattern for Paddock's own paired add/edit forms rather than full-page navigation for what is fundamentally a quick edit.

name: Natural Language Support: Best Practices
apex: Guardrails for phrasing natural-language report requests: stick to declarative report settings (filters, sorts, highlights, breaks, one grouping or calculation at a time) and avoid open-ended analytical questions or multi-level nested aggregations.
attributes: One grouping or calculation per request
workflow: Guide end users to phrase requests as direct report-setting commands rather than analytical questions; the AI only applies existing report capabilities, it does not reason over the data.
relevance: Concrete scope guardrails worth copying into Paddock's own AI-search placeholder text and into what its natural-language filter explicitly refuses to attempt server-side.

name: BLOB Columns Excluded by Wizards
apex: A report-creation wizard silently omits any BLOB column from the generated report definition; a BLOB must be added back manually afterward as a Download BLOB or Display Image typed column.
workflow: After running a report wizard over a table with a BLOB column, manually add a column expression and set its Type to Download BLOB or Display Image.
relevance: A specific wizard behavior gotcha for Oracle table-bound reports; Paddock's data model has no raw DB BLOB columns for a wizard to silently skip.

name: Automatic File Browse Binding for BLOB Columns
apex: Any form item whose source is a database BLOB column automatically becomes a File Browse item: on insert the chosen file loads into the column, on update a download link appears beside the Browse button.
attributes: Automatic Type: File Browse on BLOB-sourced items
workflow: Build a form on a table with a BLOB column and APEX renders that item as File Browse with no extra configuration.
relevance: Convenient default wiring specific to Oracle BLOB columns; Paddock's file-upload fields would bind to an object-storage URL field instead, with its own default widget.
